chapter: The union and the 1920s-30s band scene
title: Lester Young and his father, next door to the union
summary: Howard recalls Mr. Young living next door to the union and making Lester learn to read; he knew Lester before Basie and heard him practising.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Let's just see if there's anybody else through that period that I can think about and would like to ask about. Okay, what do you remember about Lester Young, because --
Well, Lester Young came here -- he came here. I don't know, he got a band somewhere, (inaudible) who was with the band. Oh, Mr. Young's -- his father, we called him Mr. Young.
The father.
And he lived up there by the union.
Next door.
Next door to the union. And he played -- I can't say what he played, Buddy.
(Inaudible.) The father?
Yeah.
Was he a coronet player? I don't remember, either.
No, he wasn't a coronet player.
He wasn't?
Uh-uh.
He didn't play piano, did he?
No, he played a guitar, I think.
He played everything.
Yeah, a little bit of everything.
He was really strong on him. There were (inaud) times Lester was talking about the father and he caught him when he couldn't read, and he really --
He did, he got ahold --
-- (inaudible) when Lester was just using his ear, which he probably was at the time.
Yeah, I think Lester was using his ear, but --
(Inaudible) learned to read.
Yeah, he made him learn. Yeah, he was using his ear, too, a lot. But he could play.
Do you remember when you first met Lester? Was he always a tenor player or was he playing alto or did he play the piano, anything like that?
No, he didn't play piano, he didn't play alto.
You met him before he got with Basie, though, didn't you?
Oh, yeah, before he got with Basie? Sure.
When was that? That's what I'd like
to know.
When was it?
Because that's the only thing I know, when he was with Basie. I didn't know anything before that.
Oh, you didn't?
No.
Oh, sure.
Do you remember who he played with before that?
Played by himself. In other words, he was with a group that I played with, and everything.
He was in groups with you, too?
Yeah.
And was he always like a strong soloist like that? Even in the beginning?
At the beginning, he was a strong soloist, played good, yeah.
Very creative.

Uh-huh. But I didn't play too much with him. I don't want to say something that's wrong. I didn't play too much. Oh, I know, I heard him play. He lived right next door to the union. That's where he was, and he'd practice out there, you'd hear him practicing in the daytime. You know, Buddy, it's the funniest thing, I can't -- those guys -- they come to my mind, but they go away. I don't know
I think talking about it is good, because you remember a lot of --
(End of proceedings as recorded.)
